calls: every call the recorder made to a product export (function, class constructor `new X`, instance method `X#m`) with its arguments viewed at call time, in order; an argument over 4000 bytes of JSON is stored once in the set `shared` table and referenced as {"$shared": n}
compare: mixdog-ai providers::openai decoder.rs:558-569,758-761,813-847,1091-1093 (refusal, namespace) and compat Responses codec (openai_profiles.rs:374,675; compat/profile.rs:667): feed `input.events` + `input.output` and compare `result` (stopReason, refusal, toolCalls incl. namespace) and `requests[*].body`; the preset/base rows compare `result` whole. K1 gap G1: the Responses wire is not built for OpenCode Go today.

describedValues.{\"$instance\": name, constructedWith: [: an instance of a product class, as the arguments it was constructed with
describedValues.{\"$response\": {status, statusText, hea: a fetch Response handed to the product: status, headers (in order) and the body chunks as delivered (bytes)
describedValues.{\"$stream\": [chunk...]}: an async stream the recorder handed the product, as the chunks it yields in order
describedValues.{\"callback\": name}: a function the recorder handed the product; its scripted behaviour is the case body

entry: openai-compat-responses.mjs sendCompatResponses(provider, history, model, tools, opts) on a real OpenAICompatProvider (its real SDK client) sending to the loopback endpoint, which serves the scripted events and a response.completed as SSE frames (every request head and body is recorded as it arrived), opencode-go.mjs resolveOpenCodeGoBaseURLs, openai-compat-presets.mjs OPENAI_COMPAT_PRESETS; fixtures from openai-compat-responses-parity.fixtures.mjs (nativeHistory) are inlined. Not run: a live endpoint or the SDK transport.
exclusions: no string is rewritten: the data directory is the fixed D:/mixdog-build/tmp/w22/<set> and the product tree D:/mixdog-build/tmp/b6f-tree (paths as Node produced them, Windows separators where Node wrote them): a replay maps its own temp directory to that prefix

net requests: the VALUES of the request headers x-stainless-os, x-stainless-arch and x-stainless-runtime-version (the SDK client stack writes the recording host's OS, architecture and Node version) are replaced by the marker `<recording host <header name>>` at exactly those header names; every other header is recorded and compared as it arrived
net requests: the recorder's x-bench-origin header is left out and `host` is the host of the origin the product addressed (the loopback port is random)

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: Rust entry (pub, on o1): mixdog_ai::providers::compat::CompatAdapter (compat/adapter.rs:63) with CompatChatCodec (compat/chat/mod.rs:96) / CompatResponsesCodec (compat/responses.rs:75), body builder build_body (compat/chat/encode.rs:372), driven through mixdog_ai::broker ModelBroker::send (mixdog-ai/src/broker/send.rs:75) and ProviderAdapter::attempt (mixdog-core-api/src/domain/provider.rs:1079).

replayExclusions.request headers: the whole request as it arrived is recorded and compared: method, path, EVERY header in arrival order (including host, connection, accept, accept-language, sec-fetch-mode, accept-encoding and the client library's user-agent) and the body bytes; no header is excluded from the comparison

values: exact (benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/lib/exact.mjs): every input, argument list, result and error is stored through the shared encoder; what JSON cannot hold is a {"$exact": <kind>} tag
